title: Trading strategy
author: MOSI1991

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body:
Building a genuinely mechanical strategy with AI usually splits into two very different approaches, and mixing them up is where most people go wrong. One is using AI/ML to generate signals directly (feature engineering off price/volume/fundamentals, training a model to predict direction or magnitude), which sounds appealing but is genuinely hard to keep robust since markets are non-stationary and models overfit to whatever regime they were trained on. The other, more reliable path for most people: keep the actual trading logic deterministic and rule-based (entries, exits, position sizing), and use AI only for the research/analysis layer, scanning for patterns, summarizing what's driving a move, scoring historical setups after the fact, rather than letting it make live decisions. The second approach is a lot easier to keep 'mechanical' in the sense of being testable and explainable, since you're not trying to interpret why a black-box model said buy. Profitable is a much higher bar than working though, plenty of AI-assisted strategies backtest well and then fall apart out-of-sample the same way any overfit strategy does, so walk-forward testing and out-of-sample validation matter just as much here as with a purely manual strategy.

If you want a starting point for the deterministic-execution-plus-AI-analysis split, that's basically the architecture EventTrader's built around. [https://claude.ai/artifact/VuwYE2KYrtzMdwyEpvA9wH](https://claude.ai/artifact/VuwYE2KYrtzMdwyEpvA9wH)

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: Short version from doing this: use the AI to write the code for a rule you already understand, not to invent the rule. Ask it for a strategy and you get something that fits the past beautifully and falls apart the next month. Then test it on data it never saw and paper trade it for a few weeks before any real money goes in.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: anytime. test it on months it never saw before you trust it.

comments.author: Mundane_Cicada_1427
comments.body: I’ve experimented with this quite a bit. AI is definitely useful for building mechanical strategies, especially for research, feature engineering, hypothesis generation, and turning rules into code. But I wouldn't rely on AI to simply generate a strategy and assume it's profitable. The important part is having a proper research/backtesting pipeline to validate the idea, test it across different market conditions, and then forward-test it before putting real money behind it. AI is a tool for the research process, not the edge itself.
